title: MZ Having trouble with size and resolution.

posts.author: CrazyImp
posts.body:
Hi guys! I'm planning my first-ever video game. However, I've encountered a problem with size, resolution, scales, etc. I'm planning on commissioning custom tilesets for parts of the game, but I'm confused about what 16x16, 32x32, and 48x48 are. From what I've gathered, 48x48 is the default for RMMZ and can be scaled down to 16x16, etc. When I comission do I tell the person that I want it in 48x48 style? How different would it be if I used 16x16 or 32x32? Will the decrease in detail be very visible?
For reference, the level of detail/style I am aiming for is the jrpg games found on Steam. The 18+ ones like Karryn's Prison. I haven't gotten around to sprites yet, so that can be ignored for now.
Lastly, for resolutions, what do those games use? In your opinion, which resolution is compatible or is most used when it comes to these sorts of games? I do know that there is a limit for RMMZ, and I would have to use a plugin.
Thanks!

posts.author: Rexodiak
posts.body:
Well, I do wish you used a different example lol, but the game you mentioned uses the default 48x48px tiles. The latest version of MZ came out today with a new 1280x720 resolution preset which has a more standard aspect ratio like the one in your example. Otherwise, you can also change this yourself by going into the 'System 2' tab in the database.
Seeing as you're new to the engine, I wouldn't recommend going over that, or else the UI will be too small, the maps too big, and you'll have to look into scaling the menus and zooming in on the maps, and a bunch of other custom stuff.
As for commissioning tilesets, go for 48x48. If you want to see what 32x32 looks like, lookup games made with RPG Maker VXAce.
Cheers!

posts.author: Rexodiak
posts.body:
By 1280x720 resolution update. Would that be the recommended ratio for a 48x48?
Click to expand...
1280x720 is the new optional resolution preset, yes, but keep in mind this is a
resolution
, not an aspect ratio.
It doesn't have an impact on tile size other than how many tiles will fit on the screen.
The aspect ratio (shape of the screen) of the example you provided (which I really wish I didn't have to look up again to answer this) is clearly 16:9. The screenshots have a resolution of 1920x1080, which is the standard HD resolution for most games... made outside RPG Maker.
Now, I suggested 1280x720 since it's a res in the 16:9 aspect ratio that offers a decent scale for menus and sprite size, but any resolution in 16:9 can work for you. The higher the resolution, the smaller your assets will appear on screen. Pixel art games really benefit from lower res, while image-heavy games (your example) will want a higher resolution, at the cost of having to do a lot more tweaking. If you still want 1920x1080p, just go into the System2 tab and try it out, see if you prefer it.
Is there a particular site that would have more flexibility?
Click to expand...
If you really want to use 32px tiles, that's fine, but from what I see, the game you mentioned uses 48px tiles. You can find tilesets for both sizes in several places, in the form of DLC on Steam, or Itch.io, and some other sites I'm sure. If you own VXAce, you can take those tilesets too.
Lastly, if I go for the 32x32, I assume that I'd have to change the resolution, correct?
Click to expand...
Nope! You'd just need to import the tilesets, but I gotta say, if you're a newbie just stick to the default.
I recommend trying out the tutorials (they made them easier to access now) and using the default settings for res and tile size until you're confident enough to deviate from them! Cya
